§ 01 Problem

Clarity
is care.

Dementia-care products need to support both patients and caregivers with flows that are simple, trustworthy, and easy to follow. The challenge was to structure a mobile experience that made care-related actions clearer without overwhelming either user type.

Most existing tools were either too clinical for daily caregiver use or too simplified to handle real care coordination. The product needed to be structured around user trust, clarity of next steps, and an architecture that felt safe and familiar to both sides of the care relationship.

Overview

Two user types. One product.
One architecture that serves both.

The dual-user structure — patient side and caregiver side — was the central design question. Both needed clarity, but the kind of clarity each required was different. The entire product was built around that distinction.

01 My Role

I worked as a Business Analyst and Project Manager across the full product cycle — participating in client meetings, gathering and clarifying requirements, understanding user and business needs, mapping flows, and creating a complete mobile wireframe system based on the client's requirements.

02 What I Contributed
  • Requirement gathering from client discussions
  • User flow mapping for patient and caregiver sides
  • Wireframe creation across key screens
  • Feature structure and screen-level planning
  • Product documentation support
  • Coordination across the full product cycle
03 Process

The work started in client meetings — understanding who the product was for, what caregivers actually needed day-to-day, and where clarity was breaking down in the existing experience.

I mapped the dual-user architecture (patient side vs. caregiver side), defined the core flows, and built the wireframe system from those foundations. Each screen decision was anchored in: what action does this user need to take, and what makes it harder than it should be?

04 What This Demonstrates
  • Healthcare domain BA and PM work
  • Dual-persona product structuring
  • Client requirement gathering and translation
  • Mobile wireframe architecture
  • Sensitivity to user trust and cognitive load
  • End-to-end product cycle ownership
